title: Blood-count random forest model screens for primary vitreoretinal lymphoma
summary: In a multicentre case-control study of 255 patients with primary vitreoretinal lymphoma and 292 controls, a six-feature random forest on complete blood count data had AUC 0.85 in the discovery cohort and 0.80-0.83 across validation cohorts, above the interleukin-10/interleukin-6 ratio (0.65-0.78). In a hospital cohort of 100,526 individuals, 38 lymphomas were found among 66 high-risk individuals and 2 more among 83,610 low-risk individuals, giving sensitivity 95.0% and positive predictive value 57.6%. In a community cohort of 515,326, 13 of 22 flagged individuals had the lymphoma (PPV 59.1%). Case numbers in the large cohorts are small.
ai_technology: Six-feature random forest model on complete blood count data
organization: Shanghai Medical College of Fudan University; Fudan University; Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University

evidence.tested: Multicentre validation cohorts plus hospital-based and community cohorts, with confirmed diagnoses.
evidence.unknown: Whether the large cohorts were evaluated prospectively with a frozen model, and effect on diagnosis timing; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest classified lymphoma risk from routine blood counts.
